findings.evidence: template/scripts/start_task.py:123 calls `observe_platform_lag` unconditionally after `reconcile_pending_rollout(..., defer=defer_rollout)`. A `PlatformLagError` (a RuntimeError) aborts the start with no bypass. design.md lists this as a deliberate risk, but it also affects projects whose `_src_path` is a local or non-GitHub source (the regex only accepts gh:/github.com forms).
findings.summary: The lag check is a hard failure on any GitHub, auth or metadata problem. It is not gated by the existing `--defer-rollout` escape hatch, so deferral no longer lets a task start when GitHub is unreachable or unreadable.

findings.evidence: tests/test_rollout_preflight.py diff: the class is added after lines 415-416 (`if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`). It still runs under discovery or pytest.
findings.summary: `PlatformLagTests` is defined after the `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` block. Running the file directly as a script never runs these tests.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/rollout_preflight.py `latest_platform_release`: `except ValueError` only. `gh_api` in rollout_identity.py:50 calls `subprocess.run(["gh", ...])` without handling OSError.
findings.summary: `latest_platform_release` only converts `ValueError` into `PlatformLagError`. If the `gh` binary is missing or cannot be executed, `gh_api` raises OSError/FileNotFoundError from `subprocess.run`, which escapes with a raw traceback instead of the explicit cause the spec requires.
